title: Training at the YMCA and teaching Flowers the time step
summary: At the YMCA Flowers shows his training, Green teaches him the time step his aunt taught him, and Flowers lets him use his name.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: how to fight like he did, I would be a champion or something, right. Well, that wasn't my ambition. So I didn't know what I wanted to be, and I was just trying to be head of the house, you know, because my father was away.

So anyhow he appointed me to meet him where he trained at in the YMCA down on 12th Street in Atlanta, Georgia, in the auditorium. So I went down there, and he started to doing some skipping rope, you know. You know, to box, the fighters skip the rope, you know, whew, whew, whew, wht-t, whew, and it was so pretty, the rhythms, you know.

And, oh, man, I was enjoying that myself. I was fascinated, you see. So then he said, 'So much for that.' He went over to the light bag, punching bag. He punched that. rerr-rerr-rerr-rerr, come to barbells and push them things out and on and on, he's coming; he'd run around, you know. Then he got the medicine ball, you know, and he said, 'Could you -- try to hit me with this,' you know.

It's a big leather -- leather ball, big thing, you know, and you pick it up. It wasn't so heavy, you know. You could throw it too. And that was -- he was teaching himself self -- art of self defense, right? So -- so he says, 'So much for that.' He says, 'How do you like that?' You know? And I says, 'That's fine. You hear them sounds?' You hear it while he was doing it. I said all this. I'm so excited, you know.

So he liked to make children happy, Tiger Flowers, very lovable person. Everybody loved him. So he said, 'Now, I'm ready.' He said, 'What's my first dance?' So in the meantime my Aunt Edna Bisson, she had done taught me how to do what -- what all dancers had to do at that time, know how to do. It was called a time step.

So that's what I started off to teaching him. Now, he liked that, you know. He was very pleased. So we was in there for about an hour, hour and a half or so, you know, and he was promising me this, that and the other, when I get a little older and to mention his name, and he said, 'You tell people if they ask you who you are, you say you're a little Tiger Flowers, you know, and you'll always have respect, you see?'
